subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram onboarding replace pairing with a token-verified first-owner allowlist bootstrap, and what compatibility policy should apply to existing installations?
rationale: The change alters the first-contact authorization boundary and setup recovery behavior; implementation cannot safely choose whether pairing remains the default or how an owner is authenticated without maintainer intent.

options.title: Token-verified first-owner bootstrap
options.body: For new Telegram onboarding, issue an expiring challenge token and write allowlist mode only after the matching sender responds, while leaving existing explicit pairing configurations unchanged.

options.title: Retain pairing as the default
options.body: Keep the present approval-based first-owner flow and improve setup guidance or optional preseeded allowlist support instead of changing the default.

options.title: Require preconfigured owner identity
options.body: Offer an explicit setup input for a known numeric owner ID and avoid inbound owner capture entirely.

recommendation.title: Token-verified first-owner bootstrap
recommendation.body: For new Telegram onboarding, issue an expiring challenge token and write allowlist mode only after the matching sender responds, while leaving existing explicit pairing configurations unchanged.
